top_choice_rationale: The magic-wavelength optical lattice clock (Katori, Ye) is a mature, independently reproduced measurement advance: JILA, RIKEN, PTB, NIST and SYRTE build and compare clocks at the 1e-18 level, and it has already delivered millimetre-scale gravitational redshift tests and tight limits on varying constants. The two-name allocation is clean and the citation scoped to the lattice clock leaves the 2005 comb and 2012 ion-clock prizes untouched. The remaining reservations, namely precision versus discovery and priority against Lemonde's group, are real but do not outweigh a result this well confirmed. Twisted bilayer graphene (P001) is a strong second: a prediction followed by experimental confirmation of a new control knob, but the field is younger, the pairing mechanism is open and the three-name attribution forces a contested cut. I would still award it over no award.
recusal_note: none apparent from profile; astroparticle and detector work has no direct link to atomic clocks or twisted graphene, though I deferred to atomic-physics colleagues on the clock priority record
